topics.label: Lecture Introduction and Objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic provides the administrative opening and learning objectives for the final lecture on cancer therapy.

topics.label: Conventional Modalities and Cytotoxic Chemotherapy
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain standard non-targeted cancer treatments including surgery, radiotherapy, and cytotoxic drugs alongside their clinical toxicities and efflux-mediated resistance mechanisms.

topics.label: Exploiting Intrinsic Cancer Cell Vulnerabilities
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine therapeutic strategies that selectively target tumors by exploiting their hormone receptor dependencies, cell cycle checkpoint losses, and DNA repair deficiencies.

topics.label: Oncogenic Kinase Inhibitors and Resistance Mechanisms
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics focus on designing small-molecule inhibitors against hyperactive driver kinases and addressing the cellular mechanisms that lead to drug resistance and addiction.

topics.label: Monoclonal Antibody and Conjugate Therapies
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics discuss antibody-mediated cancer therapies that function by directly blocking receptor signaling, triggering immune cytotoxicity, or delivering linked cytotoxic agents.

topics.label: Immunotherapy and T-Cell Engagement
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore approaches for harnessing adaptive immunity against tumors through checkpoint blockade, neoantigen recognition, bispecific engagers, and engineered CAR T cells.

topics.label: Clinical Progress, Challenges, and Future Perspectives
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics synthesize the overarching challenges, historical survival trends, and future dilemmas in optimizing cancer detection and therapy.
